pages.text: The $(thing)Tobacco Drying Rack$() turns raw leaf into cured leaf. A rack holds up to $(item)16$() identical raw leaves. The wooden frame now fits completely inside one block again, while keeping the same shared $(item)16-leaf$() capacity. Blocks can be placed normally directly above it, and inspection shows the live $(item)X/16 Leaves$() count.

pages.title: Tobacco Drying Rack
pages.text: Craft the rack before choosing a curing environment.

Right-click the rack with raw tobacco to add one leaf. Empty-hand right-click removes the batch. Sneak-right-click reports detailed status. The visible rack progresses through empty, low, medium, and full load models. Once curing reaches $(item)10%$(), the batch locks and no more leaves may be added until it is removed or finished.
pages.title: Loading the Rack

pages.text: The rack automatically chooses the strongest valid method each tick in this order: $(thing)Fire → Flue → Sun → Air$(). You do not select a mode in a menu; the structure and environment select it for you. With Create installed, one fan airflow path reaching the rack can assist a valid wooden-rack cure.
pages.title: Automatic Method
Industrial Drying Rack
pages.text: With $(thing)Create$() installed, the $(item)Industrial Drying Rack$() is a true two-block, 32-leaf automation-only factory rack. Both levels share one inventory, and valid automated input may enter from above or the horizontal sides. Curing requires matching airflow across $(thing)both$() rack levels from two distinct Encased Fans; one fan or one-sided airflow is not enough. Plain airflow normally gives Air Curing, or Sun Curing when the normal sunlight rules are also valid.

pages.title: Traditional Alternative
pages.text: A Drying Rack is not required. Sneak-right-click the underside of a sturdy block while holding 16 matching raw or cured leaves to make a traditional hanging bunch. In Creative mode, one held leaf is enough to place the 16-leaf bunch. Raw bunches cure by the same methods; cured bunches can be hung for decoration/storage but expose no inventory automation or Display Link.

The wooden rack accepts valid raw leaves from its $(thing)top or horizontal sides$(). A hopper underneath extracts only after curing is complete. Hoppers are only one option: compatible Create/NeoForge logistics can use the rack's validated input and finished-output rules, and the block space directly above the wooden rack remains free.
